title: Choose how the GSBC app is organised
question: Three ways to lay out the app around the same brand and content. Pick one to build, steer it, or ask for another three.

options.label: The week
options.lineage: the church's weekly rhythm, set like a timetable
options.thesis: Home is the church week: a day rail and an agenda where services, events, new sermons and the bulletin sit on the day they happen.
options.viewport: Brand bar, a seven-day rail with today marked, then today-onward agenda rows with times in a fixed column; four tabs: Week, Sermons, Prayer, More.
options.risk: Quiet weeks look empty; it leans on events data that is still being redone.

options.label: The bulletin
options.thesis: Home is this Sunday's bulletin, read like the paper one: a masthead, section tabs, and the outline you write notes against.
options.viewport: Navy masthead with the yearly theme, sticky tabs (Welcome, Sermons, This week, Give), then the welcome letter; tabs: Sunday, Sermons, Events, More.
options.risk: Midweek, a page about last Sunday can feel stale until the next bulletin lands.

options.label: Watch and listen
options.thesis: Home leads with the latest service to watch or listen to, picks up where you left off, and keeps this week as a compact strip below.
options.viewport: A full-width latest-service player (Live when streaming), a continue-listening row with progress, series shelves, then a this-week strip; tabs: Listen, This week, Prayer, More.
options.risk: Puts sermons above everything else, which tips away from the even mix you asked for.
